title: Follow the Cash! Microstructure of Repo Markets
gist: NY Fed researchers trace cash through the $13 trillion+ U.S. repo market: MMFs lend via tri-party (BNY Mellon), dealers intermediate, and hedge funds (about $3 trillion of repo in 2025:Q4) borrow bilaterally, often at zero haircut. Central clearing is growing, with MMF-dealer repo near 40 percent cleared in 2026:Q1 and hedge fund-dealer repo at 30 percent, ahead of the SEC's June 2027 Treasury clearing mandate.

insights.claim: U.S. repo markets exceed $13 trillion in size, versus roughly $200 billion of daily volume across federal funds, Eurodollar and selected deposit markets, making repo by far the largest short-term funding market.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Stress in repo plumbing can transmit far faster and wider than in the money markets that policy rate discussions focus on.
insights.quote: recent estimates of the size of repo markets in the U.S. exceed $13 trillion

insights.claim: Collateral broadens the motives for repo beyond cash investment: hedge funds use repo to secure specific securities while money market funds use it to reduce investment risk, which attracts a wider participant base and drives customization of clearing and settlement.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous motives explain why the market stays fragmented and why a single reform (e.g. mandated clearing) reshapes segments unevenly.
insights.locator: The role of collateral is a key feature

themes.theme: Dealers as hubs and balance-sheet intermediation

insights.claim: Dealers intermediate repo by borrowing cash from creditworthy lenders such as government MMFs and lending to riskier borrowers such as levered hedge funds, earning the rate spread (10 basis points in the authors' stylized example) as compensation for counterparty, collateral and, to a lesser extent, maturity transformation risk.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Dealer profitability and capacity hinge on balance-sheet cost, so regulatory balance-sheet constraints directly set repo spreads and leverage availability.
insights.quote: Dealers are the hubs through which repo markets flow
insights.locator: Intermediation Is Key in Repo Markets

insights.claim: In late 2024 dealers borrowed $3.7 trillion and lent $3.4 trillion per day in repo.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: The daily flow concentrated in a few dealer balance sheets shows how much system liquidity depends on their capacity.

themes.theme: Central clearing trade-offs and the SEC mandate

insights.claim: Central clearing through FICC lets dealers net positions, cutting balance-sheet costs, expanding intermediation capacity, and providing anonymity and lower counterparty risk, but it requires default fund contributions and higher margining.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Clearing shifts cost from balance sheet to margin and default-fund liquidity, so the mandate increases demand for collateral and liquidity buffers.
insights.quote: A key benefit of central clearing is the greater opportunity for netting of positions
insights.locator: Intermediation Is Key in Repo Markets

insights.claim: By June 2027 the SEC will require central clearing of U.S. Treasury repos where at least one counterparty is a direct member of a registered clearing agency, under a 2023 rule.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: A dated regulatory deadline implies a further large migration of bilateral and tri-party volume into FICC, with margin and funding implications around it.
insights.locator: Intermediation Is Key in Repo Markets

insights.claim: Migration of MMF-to-dealer repo into central clearing over the past three years, reaching almost 40 percent of MMF repo activity in 2026:Q1, is read by the authors as evidence that the benefits of clearing now outweigh the added costs for dealers.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: The historically uncleared MMF leg is being pulled into clearing ahead of the mandate, so FICC concentration risk and margin demands are rising.
insights.quote: reaching almost 40 percent of MMF repo activity in 2026:Q1

themes.theme: Lender side: MMFs and tri-party settlement

insights.claim: Money market funds are the main repo cash lenders; government MMFs hold over 80 percent of U.S. MMF assets as of March 2026 and are limited by SEC Rule 2a-7 to cash, government securities and government-backed repo.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: MMF asset flows are a primary driver of repo cash supply, so MMF inflows or outflows move funding conditions for dealers and leveraged investors.

insights.claim: MMFs do not want possession of specific collateral, so they invest in general collateral repo and outsource collateral management to a clearing bank (currently Bank of New York Mellon) in the tri-party segment, where the bank acts only as agent and does not transform counterparty risk.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Single-clearing-bank concentration in tri-party is an operational chokepoint for the largest cash lenders.
insights.quote: they typically invest in general collateral repos and rely on a clearing bank

insights.claim: Dealers accept forgoing central clearing on MMF trades because MMFs provide competitive, deep and reliable funding.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Funding reliability can outweigh netting benefits, which is why the uncleared legacy persisted.

themes.theme: Borrower side: hedge funds, bilateral repo and netted packages

insights.claim: Dealers are the main cash lenders to hedge funds, whose outstanding repo volume reached $3 trillion in 2025:Q4.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Hedge fund repo leverage of this size ties fixed-income relative-value strategies to dealer balance-sheet capacity.

insights.claim: Hedge funds prefer bilateral settlement because levered strategies such as the cash-futures basis trade need flexible access to collateral and cost efficiency to profit from small price differentials, and bilateral haircuts are lower: 75 percent of non-centrally cleared bilateral Treasury repo trades have zero haircut.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Zero haircuts imply very high leverage in basis trades, so clearing mandates that impose margin could force deleveraging or higher trade costs.
insights.quote: 75 percent of all Treasury repo trades in the bilateral segment that are non-centrally cleared have a zero haircut

insights.claim: Netted packages, pairing a reverse repo and a repo with the same counterparty and tenor, such as buying a cheap off-the-run security while sourcing an on-the-run security to short, can earn balance-sheet netting without a central counterparty, sustaining the bilateral segment.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Contracting workarounds can blunt the clearing mandate's effect on bilateral volume, making post-2027 migration less than complete.

insights.claim: Centrally cleared repo between hedge funds and dealers rose from 8 percent in early 2021 to 30 percent in late 2025, and this activity tends to rise at quarter-ends when dealer balance sheets are more constrained.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Quarter-end clearing spikes show balance-sheet scarcity driving behaviour, a signal for watching quarter-end funding pressure.
insights.quote: from 8 percent in early 2021 to 30 percent in late 2025

insights.claim: U.S. repo segments reflect participants weighing costs differently: settlement costs produced tri-party repo, balance-sheet costs favor central clearing, and creative contracting such as netted packages reduces costs in bilateral uncleared repo.
insights.speaker: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
insights.so_what: Reforms that change one cost (balance sheet, margin, settlement) will reroute volume across segments rather than just shrink it.
insights.quote: Costs related to the settlement of securities led to the emergence of tri-party repo

source_meta.author: Gara Afonso, Jun-Davinci Choi, Gonzalo Cisternas, and Will Riordan
